frontier.hypothesis: ROUTE B (PRIMARY, never attempted): shrink cam's live length from 66 into [34,38] and const's from 62 into [L(cam),38], leaving copy_end alone at L38, closing the chain from the score-10 chassis.
frontier.mechanism: Assignment is pure priority order and priority is 30000/L at nrefs=3, so the target permutation is reached by lowering the two long-lived invariants under copy_end rather than lifting copy_end over them. cam and const are loop-invariant values held across the retry loop; their surplus is the span from their hoisted defs to their last uses (cam's is the cdrom_BcdToFrames call, const's is the final func_800372F4 call).

frontier.mechanism: Live lengths are measured on the post-sched1 stream while the emitted byte order is set by sched2, so two C forms with byte-identical output can present different pre-RA live lengths. tools/sched_solver models both scheduler passes order- and clock-exactly and has never been pointed at this function.

frontier.hypothesis: ROUTE A reopens only if copy_end's L38 cap is a flow-counting artifact rather than a last-use fact.
frontier.mechanism: reg_live_length counts per-insn live VISITS accumulated over propagate_block iterations, so a value that is loop-carried can score far above its linear span (const reaches 76 in a function whose pre-RA stream is much shorter). If copy_end is being counted in fewer block visits than its loop-carried liveness implies, the cap is soft.
frontier.next_probe: From the same per-function-segmented flowdbg data, compare copy_end's per-block visit counts against const's block-for-block.
